fields.h1: Build a Return Authorization Form Template With RA Numbers
fields.hero_description: Build a return authorization form template that checks each order's return window and emails an RA number when it passes.
fields.features_heading: Every Return Request, Checked Against the Order
fields.features_subheading: A downloaded template collects a request and stops. Here, the app reads the order behind it and numbers the return.
fields.feature_1:
Describe your policy, get the form behind it

Describe your return policy and the products it covers. Emergent builds the request form, the returns table and the staff dashboard, then changes them when you prompt again.
fields.feature_2:
Order details pulled in, not retyped

Connect the store platform your orders run through. The customer types an order number, and the app reads the items and the delivery date through that platform's API.
fields.feature_3:
Questions that follow the reason picked

Pick damaged in transit and the form asks which part broke. Pick wrong item and it asks what arrived instead. Changed my mind skips both and goes to the return address.
fields.feature_4:
RA numbers your dock can match

Each approved request takes the next number in the series and prints it on the return instructions. At the dock, typing that number opens the request beside its order.
fields.feature_5:
A Slack ping when a person has to decide

Requests that fail a rule wait in a review list, and Slack or email tells the right person, with a link to the request. Customer names and addresses stay in the database.
fields.feature_6:
Your returns data, your database

Every request, decision and inspection result lands in a database you own, with no cap on responses. On paid plans, export the full code to your own GitHub repository.
fields.why_description: Emergent builds the returns app from a plain-English description of your policy. The free tier covers building and publishing it.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Returns and What Happens Next
fields.tab_content_1:
When a cracked lid is reported on day 9

Gwyneira Branscombe's Dutch oven from Hearthwell Cookware arrives with a cracked lid. She opens the return form 9 days after delivery, types her order number, and picks damaged in transit. Her order sits inside the store's 30-day window. The app issues RA-1047 and emails it to her with the address to ship the pot to.
fields.tab_content_2:
On day 44, brake sets wait for a support lead

Osmund Treadwell runs a bike shop and asks Copperbrook Cycle Supply to take back 6 brake sets 44 days after delivery. The policy allows 30 days, and the app holds the request without a number. Support lead Lisbeth Marchetti-Ross gets a Slack message with a link and decides whether this one earns an exception.
fields.tab_content_3:
With all parts in, a $240 tent earns $204

A $240 tent reaches Stonechat Outdoor's dock with RA-2290 on the label. Ines Coldharbour types the number, counts the poles and stakes, and marks it opened with all parts present. Stonechat takes 15% off opened items as a restocking fee. The record shows $36 off and a $204 store credit waiting for a manager.
fields.tab_content_4:
One reason behind 11 of 18 returns: runs small

Brightwater Footwear's October report groups every return request by product and the reason picked. The Trail Runner leads with 18 returns, and 11 of 18 returns say runs small. The rest split between damage in transit and a change of mind. The product team adds a sizing note to the listing that week.

fields.howto_title: How to Build a Return Authorization Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to set up a return authorization form template that checks each request and numbers approved returns.
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Connect the store that holds orders
fields.howto_step_1_des: Put the policy in plain words: how many days after delivery a customer can ask, and which items you never take back. Each line becomes a rule the form checks before it issues a number.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Give customers a short list of reasons to pick from, such as damaged in transit or wrong item. Decide which reasons need more detail, and the form asks for it only when that reason is picked.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Pick a prefix and a starting number, such as RA-1000. Print the number on the return instructions and ask customers to write it on the box. The dock then matches each package to its request in one search.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Link the shop where orders are placed. An order number then brings up its delivery date and items. Try one real order number first and check that the dates match what the shop shows.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Name the person who decides on requests that fail a rule, such as a late request or an item you do not normally take back. Pick whether that person hears about it in Slack or by email.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Set the checks your dock runs
fields.howto_step_6_des: Write the checks your dock runs on a returned item and the condition labels staff can choose. Tie each label to an outcome, such as full credit for unopened items or a restocking fee for opened ones.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test one request of each kind
fields.howto_step_7_des: Submit a request inside the window, one past it, and one for a wrong item. Read each email the way a customer would, then delete the test records before the first real request arrives.

faq_plan.q: What is a return authorization form template?
faq_plan.a: A return authorization form template is the request a customer fills in to ask permission to send a product back. TechTarget defines an RMA as a numbered authorization provided by a mail-order or e-commerce merchant to permit the return of a product. The form collects what that decision needs: the order number, the item, the reason, and an email address.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a return authorization form template?
faq_plan.a: Describe your return policy to Emergent's AI form builder in plain English: the window in days, the reasons customers can pick and the number format you want. You get a working app to test, not a blank document. Then connect your store so each request can read its order, and send a few test requests before customers see it.

faq_plan.q: What fields should a return authorization form template include?
faq_plan.a: Include the order number, the item being returned, the reason, the outcome the customer wants, and an email address for the RA number. Skip what the order already holds, such as the shipping address. An app built with Emergent can connect to your store through its API and read those details from the order.

faq_plan.q: Should a return authorization form template ask for card details?
faq_plan.a: No. Keep card numbers off the return form, because the order already records how the customer paid and the refund goes back through that payment. If you need permission to charge a card later, for a late fee or a replacement, collect it on a separate credit card authorization form that the customer signs for that purpose.

faq_plan.q: Does a return authorization form template need a tracking number field?
faq_plan.a: Yes, add one for after the customer ships. An RA number is the approval you give for one return; a tracking number is the carrier's label for one package. The RA number tells your dock which request a box belongs to, while the tracking number tells you where that box is. With both on one record, staff can answer where is my return without opening the carrier site.

faq_plan.q: What should a return authorization form template say about boxes sent without a number?
faq_plan.a: It should say what you do with them, in the instructions customers read before they ship. Per TechTarget, products that are returned without an RMA can be refused or subject to a restocking fee by the retailer. Pick one of those outcomes, print it on your returns page, and give the dock a label to log an unnumbered box under.

faq_plan.q: Can a return authorization form template handle partial returns?
faq_plan.a: Yes. List each item on the order with a quantity box, and the RA number covers only the items the customer picks. The rest stay on the order as kept. Emergent builds that item list from your prompt, and you can change the rules for multi-item orders later by prompting again.

faq_plan.q: Can a return authorization form template track a return after approval?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Give each request a status that moves with the package: issued, shipped, received, inspected, and closed. Staff change the status at each handoff, and the customer gets an email when the dock receives the box. Every status change is kept in a database you own. Sort by date to find the returns that have sat at one stage for more than a week.

faq_plan.q: Can a return authorization form template offer exchanges as well as refunds?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Add a question that asks which outcome the customer wants, and show follow-up fields only for the one picked: a new size or color for an exchange, nothing extra for store credit. Staff see the choice on the request before the box arrives and can set a replacement aside early.

faq_plan.q: How should reasons be phrased in a return authorization form template?
faq_plan.a: Phrase each reason the way a customer would say it, such as arrived damaged or too small, and keep the list to the reasons you act on differently. A reason that changes nothing about the outcome or the report can go. Add an other option with a short text box, and read those answers each month for reasons to add.
